articles.title: A Handmade Moon Can Fool the Camera
articles.summary: A crater made on a tabletop can look surprisingly real. National Geographic Kids explains how plaster models and careful drawings can turn the moon into an art project.

articles.title: Finding a Movie’s Perfect Place Is Its Own Adventure
articles.summary: A junkyard one day, a fancy hotel the next: finding film locations can reveal surprising parts of New York. Director Paula González-Nasser turned her scouting experience into The Scout.

articles.title: A Writer’s Life Is Heading From Book to Screen
articles.summary: A biography can become the starting point for a movie. Higher Ground and Anonymous Content plan a film based on Nicholas Boggs’s book about writer James Baldwin.
